findings:
🟠 [test-oracle-integrity] MUST-FIX The depth-0 acceptance oracle `groups.test.ts` was modified, and `fanout.test.ts` is another pre-existing test changed outside the two explicitly allowed files; this bypasses the frozen verification boundary. Restore both pre-existing tests exactly and place any additional coverage in new test files.
🟠 [peers-sql-scope] MUST-FIX `/v1/peers` selects every enabled human and every peer membership before filtering them in JavaScript, violating the required SQL-WHERE membership enforcement and making work/timing depend on inaccessible records. Restrict both visible peers and returned `groups[]` in SQL using the reader's memberships.
🟠 [legacy-wire-compat] MUST-FIX Legacy responses are no longer byte-identical: claim acquire/list results now expose `group_id`, and `/v1/peers` always adds `groups`. Preserve the old response shapes in legacy mode and expose group fields only in strict mode.
🟠 [refusal-audit-gaps] MUST-FIX Several post-group-resolution refusals, including address-rule failures such as `sender_instance_required` and `direct_needs_instance`, return without an audit containing `group_id`. Route all such refusals through an audited response helper carrying the resolved group.
🟠 [message-order-alias] MUST-FIX Strict `/v1/messages` normalizes and audits `@team` before capability and recipient-membership enforcement, contrary to the mandated sequence; rejected unknown-group or cap-denied requests therefore create a premature `deprecated_team_alias` side effect. Move normalization and its audit after capability/recipient enforcement.
